mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -39.6% to -21.3% over four weeks, signaling sustained recovery momentum. This trend will continue over the next four weeks, producing net positive change in RETAIL_REC relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:monotonic improvement from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines by more than 5 percentage points in any single week over the next four weeks, or mean RETAIL_REC over weeks t+1 to t+4 is lower than mean over t-3w to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains suppressed at -23.0% (t-0w), indicating continued remote work adoption. This persistent workplace absence will constrain retail footfall during commute windows and lunch periods, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed below current levels over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -20% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -15% in any week t+1 to t+4, or RETAIL_REC mean over t+1 to t+4 exceeds mean over t-3w to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage has stabilized around -54% to -58%, indicating constrained commuting capacity. When TRANSIT rises by more than 8 percentage points week-on-week, it signals reopening of transport infrastructure that enables retail access, driving RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 8 percentage points in any single week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT range t-3w to t-0w is -66.0% to -54.1%
failure_condition: TRANSIT does not rise more than 8 percentage points in any week t+1 to t+2, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase by at least 3 percentage points within two weeks of such a TRANSIT rise.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has converged toward baseline (-1.3% at t-0w), indicating essential retail normalization. When GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes within 2 percentage points of baseline, policy restrictions on non-essential retail relax, permitting RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.

failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM does not stabilize within -2% to +2% for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC mean over t+1 to t+4 is lower than over t-3w to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from +16.0% to +8.4%, indicating residents are spending less time at home. This outbound shift, combined with PARKS remaining suppressed at -14.0%, suggests outdoor recreation constraints are easing and residents are redirecting to indoor retail venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below +10% AND PARKS rises above -10%
failure_condition: Both conditions not met simultaneously in any week t+1 to t+4, or RETAIL_REC mean over t+1 to t+4 does not exceed mean over t-3w to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: November-to-December seasonal patterns typically drive retail recovery as holiday shopping begins. RETAIL_REC's current trajectory of +18.3 percentage point improvement over four weeks will accelerate in the next four weeks due to seasonal demand, producing further net positive change in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 18.3 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over t+1 to t+4 is lower than or equal to mean over t-3w to t-0w, or weekly RETAIL_REC declines in more than two weeks of the next four weeks.

When both series rise simultaneously by more than 5 percentage points in the same week, it signals coordinated reopening of work and transport infrastructure, triggering retail recovery within one week.

evidence_refs: fact:both series severely suppressed at t-0w
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not rise more than 5 percentage points in the same week during t+1 to t+4, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase within one week of such a synchronized rise.

If PARKS rises above -5% while RESIDENTIAL remains above +8%, residents will substitute outdoor recreation for indoor retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
